correctness.rationale: In the pure single-operation language completeness gives the sole 0-type. Idempotence reduces every one-variable term to that variable, so QE gives exactly one 1-type. If x≠y, then z=x·y is distinct from both by the Steiner inverse identity and commutativity; x·z=y and y·z=x. Together with idempotence this closes the three normal forms and determines all atomic equalities. If x=y every term reduces to x instead. Both equality patterns are realized (the published theorem already guarantees a nontrivial model); QE gives exactly two complete 2-types. Barbina–Casanovas Theorem 3.3 supplies continuum many complete empty-set 3-types of this very theory. For n>3 the tuple obtained by repeating the first variable induces an injection of the complete 3-type space, and a countable language has only countably many formulas in the given finite tuple, giving the matching upper bound. Read the frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py without running the script: the finite example checks the table on three elements, not QE, the continuum lower bound, or the universal inference from the identities.
